questions.prompt: Which of these places would you prefer to go to with friends, and why?

segments.text: I would prefer to go to the café with my friends.
It is easy to talk when you are sitting at a table, and you don't have to carry a lot of things. Also, a café is a good idea when it rains.
Last weekend, for example, my friends and I had hot chocolate at a café and talked for two hours.
I'd go for the café, I think, although the picnic looks lovely on a sunny day.
In a café you can chat for hours without worrying about the weather, and there is no need to carry food, a blanket or anything else.
Having said that, a picnic would be much cheaper, so I might suggest it for a big group of friends in summer.

questions.prompt: How often do you meet friends or family to eat together?

segments.text: I meet my family to eat together almost every Sunday.
We have lunch at my grandparents' house, and my grandmother cooks a big meal for everybody. With my friends, I usually go out for dinner once or twice a month.
Last Sunday, for example, we ate paella and then played cards all afternoon.
I think it is important to spend time with the people you love.
Pretty often: it's a Sunday tradition in my family to have lunch together at my grandparents' house.
My grandmother cooks enough to feed an army, and we usually end up playing cards all afternoon. I see my friends for dinner about twice a month, which is as often as our busy lives allow.
For me, those shared meals are what makes a week feel complete.

questions.prompt: Which of these places do you prefer for learning something new, and why?

segments.text: I prefer to learn something new in a class with a teacher.
A teacher can explain things in a simple way, and I can ask questions at any time. I also like learning with other people because it is more fun.
For example, I started a guitar course last year, and my classmates helped me a lot.
At home, I often get tired and stop.
On the whole I'd choose the classroom, because I learn best when I can talk to a teacher.
Someone can explain a difficult point straight away, and listening to other people's questions often teaches me things I would never have thought of myself.
That said, reading at home is better for reviewing, because I can go at my own pace without any pressure.
